input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton textile, a long horizontal running border, photographed flat and straight-on so the painted cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge with no margin. Subject: the same lotus-and-vine scroll used in the border of the reference image, scaled up large so that exactly six big lotus blossoms span the width, each blossom nearly half the height of the band. A single continuous ecru vine undulates in one smooth sine wave from left to right; in each of its six curves sits one large open lotus blossom in ecru with madder-red dotted petals, alternating above and below the vine, with a few small curling tendrils, one bud and two green leaves per curve. This is a simple, bold, rhythmic border, not a dense allover pattern: generous areas of plain madder-red ground show between the motifs. The ground is dyed deep madder red. A thin ecru band of black dots runs along the full top edge and another along the full bottom edge. The scroll runs off both the left and right ends of the frame with no end border. Style: match the reference image exactly in palette, line quality, fill patterns and cotton texture. Freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, no signature, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames.
